copy.blurb:
FIFA World Cup 2026 on Saturday, evening UTC kickoff, brings Qatar and Switzerland together. The Desk's read disagrees with the market on the Qatar side, by +12.4pp — and that disagreement is the Pick.

Elo numbers going in: Qatar 1640, Switzerland 1830. That's a 190-point lead for Switzerland — closer than a casual reader of the market price might assume. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. The adjustment layer is quiet on this fixture — no host bonus, no home-ground correction, no altitude folding in. The Elo numbers above are what the model uses.

Three-way split from the model: Qatar to win at 20%, the draw at 19%, and Switzerland to win at 61%. The Desk publishes a three-way read against the same W/D/L resolution Polymarket and Kalshi settle on — not a scoreline guess. Qatar sits at 20% of the mass.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Qatar to win at 8%, the draw at 16%, and Switzerland to win at 76%. Polymarket has Qatar at 8%, which prices out at American odds of +1142; the model has the same side at 20%. The +12.4pp gap across them is the disagreement we're surfacing.

The +3pp Pick threshold isn't on the point estimate, it's on the 5th-percentile from a 100-sample bootstrap of the Elo prior plus bonuses. On Qatar, that haircut lands the model at 15%; the market is at 8%. Even on the conservative reading, the gap is +6.8pp. The point is selection, not a blanket call. Most matches the model and the market agree on. This is one of the ones where they don't, and the gap is on the Qatar side specifically.

The read above is the most recent one, not a frozen call. With kickoff 18 days out, refresh is weekly; daily cadence picks up inside the final five days. Injury news, the actual XI, and conditions at kickoff all change what the model sees. We re-publish on every refresh. The page shows what the engine reads; what to do with that information is a reader's call.
drivers: Bootstrap lower-bound on the Qatar side still clears the Pick threshold.
Editorial analysis only — Odds Primer does not place trades or recommend a wager.
Pre-match Elo gives Qatar a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +12.4pp gap clears the Desk's 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
copy.summary: The model thinks Qatar are mispriced. Our number reads 20% on the home side; the market reads 8%. The +12.4pp gap is the Pick.
copy.title: Qatar v Switzerland · the model leans Qatar
